description: Machine-readable selection, composition, delivery, ownership, and accessibility metadata for Kerf UI and its supported Web Awesome set.

entries.name: Badge
entries.description: Self-styled, non-interactive status, count, and category metadata configured through semantic tone, appearance, shape, and size props.
entries.purpose: Present compact metadata without application-authored badge CSS or consumer styling of component internals.
useWhen: Show a short status, count, category, or metadata label whose presentation should be configured rather than restyled.
avoidWhen: Do not use Badge as a button, link, or removable chip; choose an interactive control with the correct native semantics.
Do not rely on tone alone to communicate meaning.
variants: neutral, info, pop, success, warning, or danger tone
compact or default size, or a text-free dot (size: 'dot')
accessibility: Badge is non-interactive. Supply label when visible content is abbreviated, and ariaHidden when it repeats an accessible name owned by the surrounding component. A text-free dot must take either label (exposed as an image) or ariaHidden, which the types enforce.
Keep meaningful text visible because tone is supplementary.

entries.name: Chip
entries.description: A short tag with semantic tone and an optional accessible remove button, including compact and disabled variants.
entries.purpose: Render removable tags without application rules on Web Awesome internals.
useWhen: Show a short tag that the application can remove through a delegated action, including a compact or disabled tag.
avoidWhen: Use Badge for non-interactive status and count metadata.
Do not use the remove button without a specific accessible name.
variants: neutral, info, pop, success, warning, or danger tone
removable or plain, enabled or disabled
accessibility: The remove control is a native button and requires an action and a specific removeLabel. A disabled chip disables that button and removes it from keyboard interaction.
Keep meaningful tag text visible because tone is supplementary.

entries.name: LucideIcon
entries.description: Decorative and meaningfully labeled Lucide-compatible icons.
entries.purpose: Decorative and meaningfully labeled Lucide-compatible icons.
useWhen: Render a decorative or explicitly labeled Lucide-compatible icon in Kerf application UI.
avoidWhen: Do not use an icon as the only name of an unfamiliar action.

usageExamples.title: Solid selected glyph
usageExamples.description: The solid appearance fills a compatible Lucide glyph with currentColor while retaining its stroke and accessible name policy.

usageExamples.title: Semantic icon color
usageExamples.description: Set an icon foreground with a semantic color token; omit color to inherit from surrounding text. Use foregroundColor() for a custom CSS color or foregroundColorVar() for an app variable.

usageExamples.title: Inline with text
usageExamples.description: Let a decorative icon flow inside Text or other prose while preserving its inherited 1em size.

accessibility: Decorative icons are aria-hidden; meaningful icons require a label.

entries.name: DisclosureArrow
entries.description: Root-scaled 18px animated open and closed disclosure indicator with configurable directions, shortest-path rotation, and right-oriented replacement icon content.
entries.purpose: Indicate whether a disclosure control is open with an overridable 18px root-scaled visual and shortest-path rotation behavior.
useWhen: Add a shortest-path rotating indicator to a control that owns open and closed state; author replacement icon content facing right before direction transforms are applied.
avoidWhen: Do not use the arrow as the interactive control or accessible name by itself.
accessibility: The arrow is decorative; expose expanded state through aria-expanded on its owning control and keep that control's accessible name stable.

entries.name: Foundation tokens
entries.description: The complete public typography, spacing, breakpoint, geometry, radius, color, focus, and shadow token surface shipped by foundation.css.
entries.purpose: Provide the shared semantic token foundation for application themes and every styled Kerf UI component.
useWhen: Theme a Kerf application globally or reuse the shipped semantic typography, spacing, geometry, color, focus, and shadow values in application-owned composition CSS.
avoidWhen: Do not replace a component-specific prop or token with a broad foundation override when only one component instance should change.
appOwns: responsive policy at the cataloged device-class breakpoints
accessibility: Preserve semantic contrast relationships and the visible focus ring when overriding foundation colors.

entries.name: Document baseline
entries.description: Opt-in document-level defaults: border-box sizing, body margin/font/surface, native table-cell and form-control font metrics, link color, and the html → body → .kui-app-root full-height chain.
entries.purpose: Let an application opt into Kerf UI-owned document defaults and a definite full-height chain for a percentage-height application shell.
useWhen: An application wants Kerf UI to own document-level box sizing, body typography, native table-cell and form-control font metrics, surface, and link color.
A full-height shell (Workbench, SplitView, NavStack, or TabScaffold) mounts into one direct container: put .kui-app-root on that container.
avoidWhen: Do not put .kui-app-root on several sibling containers; each requests the full available document height.
Do not import it where the host page already owns document-level defaults it would override.

alternatives.when: Import the foundation tokens the baseline reads; the baseline itself adds only global document selectors.

appOwns: application overrides loaded after the baseline
accessibility: Links keep the semantic link color at zero specificity so application focus and link styles still apply.

notes: The body margin is removed; .kui-app-root only sets height: 100% and owns no inset.

entries.name: Application layout
entries.description: Unpadded panes, 24px content stacks, and self-contained 8/1/8 content items for application layout boundaries.
entries.purpose: Provide one reusable pane, toolbar, content stack, and content-item geometry across sidebars, main areas, and dialogs.
useWhen: Build sidebars, main areas, inspectors, or dialogs from an unpadded pane with optional toolbar/footer and one content stack.
Relocate a hidden pane's restore control into the adjacent main toolbar on the same logical edge.
avoidWhen: Do not pad the pane itself or add wrapper insets around children that already own content-item geometry.
Do not leave an empty icon-only rail after collapsing a pane.
appOwns: pane visibility and matching collapse/restore controls
variants: hidden inline-start pane restored from main-toolbar leading
hidden inline-end pane restored from main-toolbar trailing
accessibility: Keep reading and focus order coherent when controls wrap or panes relocate, and preserve one scroll owner per pane.
When collapse replaces one control with its counterpart in another toolbar, move focus to the newly rendered restore or collapse control.

entries.name: Pane
entries.description: An unpadded application column with optional vertical header/footer slots, one scrolling vertical content stack, and independent logical-edge separators.
entries.purpose: Organize a sidebar, main area, inspector, or dialog column into fixed vertical header/footer chrome around one scrolling content owner.
useWhen: An application column needs shared header, content, and optional footer organization with exactly one scrolling content owner.
A pane boundary needs an opt-in separator on any combination of logical sides.
Pinned chrome needs a divider from the scrolling content only while content is scrolled beneath it (wireScrollDividers).
A lowered background must cover the scrolling work viewport and blank space after short content without a second scroll container (appearance: sunken).
A child table or other component needs edge-to-edge decoration with text aligned to other pane content.
avoidWhen: Do not use Pane as a padded card or add a competing scroll owner around its content slot.
Do not enable separators merely as decoration; use them only where the pane owns a real boundary.

alternatives.when: Use the layout content-item and control classes inside Pane when children need shared geometry.

appOwns: which sides may compensate for device safe areas in an app-owned arrangement (safeAreaEdges)
whether the chrome dividers follow the scroll, always show, or never show (chromeDividers)
default or sunken scrolling work surface (appearance)
variants: chrome dividers only while scrolled (default, wired by wireScrollDividers)
accessibility: Choose semantic root and content elements that match the region and provide labels for landmark elements.
Keep fixed header/footer chrome outside the single scrolling content slot so reading and focus order remain coherent.

notes: The pane is unpadded; separators are independently opt-in on logical edges and default off.

Safe areas: the root and separators paint through unsafe areas while header, content, and footer pad the sides the pane still reaches (routed by --kui-edge-inset-*); content block insets are scroll padding.
The scrolling content exposes its resolved logical inline padding to descendants as --kui-pane-content-inset-inline-start/end, including safe areas and deepInset.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-divider
stateAttributes.meaning: The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which this chrome currently draws its scroll divider: the side facing the scroller while content is hidden beyond it. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: NavStack
entries.description: A controlled one-pane navigation stack that keeps prior views mounted, slides content on push and pop, cross-fades per-view chrome, and moves/restores focus.
entries.purpose: Present a single linear or drill-down flow while preserving each prior view's state, scroll position, and place in the stack.
useWhen: A compact surface shows one view at a time and navigation pushes into details or pops back.
A simple single-pane screen needs the same stable app-layout contract without any nested navigation.
avoidWhen: Do not use NavStack when a list and detail should remain visible together; use SplitView.
Do not use it for co-equal top-level destinations on compact devices; wrap one stack per destination in TabScaffold.

alternatives.when: Promote a list-to-detail stack to SplitView once both regions fit together.
Use one NavStack as each TabScaffold tab's persistent content.

appOwns: ordered view stack and stable keys
view content and structured top and bottom toolbar configurations
preferred initial focus targets when DOM order is insufficient
per-view bottom toolbar or a persistent structured fallback
per-view leading, center, and trailing top-toolbar groups
per-view header and footer with List and Pane configuration
top-toolbar defaults, title size, and heading level
whether the chrome and bottom-toolbar dividers follow the scroll, always show, or never show (chromeDividers)
variants: custom back icon or visible back text
persistent final top-toolbar group (panelToggle) when embedded in a Workbench panel
chrome and bottom-toolbar dividers only while the active view scrolls beneath them (wired by wireScrollDividers)
permanent or no chrome dividers (chromeDividers always or none)
accessibility: Give the stack region an accessible label and every back control a stable action label; visible backText names the control itself.
Set toolbarConfig.headingLevel when the view title is the page's or section's heading landmark.
Use wireNavStack so each controlled push moves focus into the new top view and each pop restores the revealed view's remembered descendant.
Mark a preferred initial heading or control with data-nav-focus when the first enabled focusable descendant is not the right target.

notes: The stack owns its full-height chrome and viewport; each view owns its internal content padding and scrollable content.

The top chrome's bottom line and the bottom toolbar's top line are scroll state (wireScrollDividers), drawn as an overlaid 1px pseudo-element on the chrome and the bottom toolbar's always-present 1px top border, so neither moves the chrome or the content.

entries.name: SplitView
entries.description: A responsive list-detail layout that shows both panes on roomy device classes and collapses to a navigation stack on compact classes.
entries.purpose: Present a selectable list and its detail together when space permits, with a one-pane drill-down replacement on compact devices.
useWhen: Selection in a primary list updates a related detail pane and both should remain visible on roomy device classes.
The same list-detail flow must become a navigation stack on a handset or portrait tablet.
avoidWhen: Do not use SplitView for a single linear flow; use NavStack.
Do not use it for a complex desktop tool with multiple peripheral panels; use Workbench.

alternatives.when: SplitView renders the one-pane navigation-stack form on compact device classes.
Use Workbench when a desktop-class tool needs more than the list and detail regions.

appOwns: optional list collapse state and its restore control
compact list and detail toolbar groups, toolbar configuration, and chrome dividers
variants: collapsed resizable list with a restore control
accessibility: Give the overall split and both meaningful panes accessible labels.
Wire the compact back action and optional separator keyboard behavior, and restore focus when controlled navigation replaces a view.

notes: The root owns the two-column split and the list pane owns its separator; list and detail content own their internal padding and scroll behavior.

entries.name: TabScaffold
entries.description: A controlled compact-device bottom tab scaffold that keeps every tab scene mounted so its navigation and scroll state survive selection changes.
entries.purpose: Switch among two to five co-equal top-level destinations on compact devices while preserving each destination's independent content state.
useWhen: A handset or portrait-tablet app has two to five co-equal top-level destinations.
Each destination must stay mounted so its NavStack and scroll position survive tab switches.
avoidWhen: Do not use TabScaffold for document tabs or reorderable work items; use TabBar.
Do not retain the bottom bar on desktop when the same destinations should be promoted to a Workbench rail or sidebar.

alternatives.when: Use TabBar and AppTab for document-style tabpanels, overflow, closing, or reordering.
Promote top-level destinations to a rail or sidebar on desktop-class layouts.

appOwns: tab badge counts or dots and their localized badgeLabel phrases
responsive replacement on larger device classes
whether the bar divider follows the scroll, always shows, or never shows (chromeDividers)
variants: bar divider only while the active scene continues below it (wired by wireScrollDividers)
permanent or no bar divider (chromeDividers always or none)
accessibility: Give the tablist an accessible label and keep exactly the active tab in the sequential focus order.
Wire selection through the controlled active id while leaving inactive scenes mounted and hidden.

A tab badge is aria-hidden; supply badgeLabel so the tab's accessible name becomes "<label>, <badgeLabel>" (it defaults to the badge text). The dot form, badge: true, has no text, so its badgeLabel is required.

notes: The scaffold owns the full-height scene region and safe-area-aware bottom bar; scene content owns its internal geometry.
The bar's top line is scroll state (wireScrollDividers): it shows only while the active scene's content continues below the bar, by coloring the bar's always-present 1px top border.

stateAttributes.meaning: The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which this chrome currently draws its scroll divider: the side facing the scroller while content is hidden beyond it. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: Workbench
entries.description: A desktop-class multi-panel workspace with independently collapsible, optionally drag-resizable left and right rails and a bottom drawer around one central work area.
entries.purpose: Arrange a complex tool or editor as a stable central work area with optional peripheral rails and a bottom drawer.
useWhen: A desktop-class tool needs a central work area plus independently collapsible navigator, inspector, or console regions.
A desktop-class tool should let people size its peripheral panels by dragging or with the keyboard; opt each panel in with resizable and wire it with wireWorkbench.
avoidWhen: Do not shrink the full multi-panel shell onto compact devices; present peripheral content through NavStack or overlay drawers instead.
Do not use Workbench for one standalone collapsible rail or drawer; use CollapsiblePanel.
Do not offer resizing where rails present as compact overlay drawers or are replaced; set a panel's responsiveOverlayAt, or pass deviceClass so wireWorkbench suspends resizing on compact classes.

alternatives.when: Use Pane inside Workbench regions when fixed header/footer chrome must surround one scroll owner.

appOwns: navigation panel view stack and push/pop actions when navStack is supplied
variants: navigation panel with per-screen toolbar, fixed header, and one scroll owner; standard toggle remains last and relocates while collapsed
opt-in drag and keyboard resizable panels with min/max limits
resizable rails that leave the work area a minimum width and shrink in proportion when the Workbench narrows
rails or a drawer that present as overlays below a narrow or compact Workbench container breakpoint
transient overlay panels wired with wireWorkbench: collapsed on entering the breakpoint, closed by Escape or an outside press
inline, overlay, or hidden responsive presentation
narrow or compact single-track responsive fill
chrome dividers only while scrolled (wired by wireScrollDividers)
accessibility: Give the Workbench and each meaningful rail or drawer an accessible label.
Keep collapse controls outside the disappearing region and move focus when a controlled rerender replaces a collapse control with its restore control.

A resizable panel's separator is a focusable role="separator" with its size in aria-valuenow and limits in aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax; arrow keys resize by 16px, Shift+arrow by 64px, and Home/End jump to the limits. It leaves the tab order while its panel is collapsed or not inline.

Given a panel's collapsed signal, wireWorkbench closes an open overlay panel on Escape or an outside press and, however the panel closed, returns focus stranded inside it to the control that opened it, else to its restore control.

An overlay panel can cover the toolbar toggle that opened it (a narrow right rail covers an editor toolbar's trailing toggle), so give every panel that may overlay its own close control in its header: a Pane header Toolbar with a single ToolbarControlGroup around the collapsiblePanelToggleIcon(side, false) button.

notes: Workbench owns the rail and drawer separators; each region's content owns its internal padding and scroll behavior.

stateAttributes.name: data-numeric-overlays
stateAttributes.meaning: Space-separated left, right, drawer, rail-open, and open tokens mirror numeric overlay state for local CSS invalidation. Absent when no numeric overlay is active.

stateAttributes.name: data-handle-inset
stateAttributes.meaning: Written by the shared resize wiring when the work-area minimum or a parent clamp holds a rail's maximum near its size. It carries no Workbench styling; the Workbench handle stays at the rail's inner edge.

stateAttributes.name: data-resizing
stateAttributes.meaning: Present on a resizable rail or the drawer while a pointer drag resizes it.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-overflow
stateAttributes.on: kui-pane__content of each panel and work-area Pane
stateAttributes.meaning: The physical edges, in canonical t/r/b/l order, beyond which content is scrolled out of view; absent when nothing is hidden (content that fits never reports its far edges). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-divider
stateAttributes.on: kui-pane__header and kui-pane__footer of each panel and work-area Pane
stateAttributes.meaning: The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which this chrome currently draws its scroll divider: the side facing the scroller while content is hidden beyond it. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: CollapsiblePanel
entries.description: A standalone controlled left or right rail or bottom drawer with standard collapse icons and optional compact-overlay behavior through wireSidebar.
entries.purpose: Add one independently collapsible peripheral panel without adopting the complete multi-panel Workbench shell.
useWhen: An application needs one collapsible side rail or bottom drawer outside a full Workbench.
The panel should become a dismissable, focus-managed overlay on compact devices.
avoidWhen: Do not use CollapsiblePanel for a complete editor shell with multiple coordinated rails and a drawer; use Workbench.
Do not preserve an empty icon-only rail when collapsed; move the restore control into adjacent visible chrome.

alternatives.when: Use Workbench when the central work area coordinates multiple peripheral panels.
Use the production recipe for collapse, restore, compact overlay, focus, and persistence ownership.

variants: chrome dividers only while scrolled (wired by wireScrollDividers)
accessibility: Give the panel region and every collapse or restore control an accessible label.
Keep the restore control outside the disappearing panel and use wireSidebar for focus transfer, Escape, backdrop dismissal, and compact focus trapping.

notes: The panel owns its dock-edge separator and size track; its child content owns internal padding and scrolling.

stateAttributes.meaning: With a deviceClass: "inline" on a wide device class, otherwise the compact presentation ("overlay" or "hidden"). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.meaning: With a deviceClass on a compact device: "true" for the overlay presentation, "false" for hidden. Absent on a wide device class. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-morph-preserve
stateAttributes.meaning: Keeps the injected compact-overlay backdrop through the application's re-render; the helper creates and removes the backdrop itself.

stateAttributes.meaning: The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which this chrome currently draws its scroll divider: the side facing the scroller while content is hidden beyond it. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: SunkenPanel
entries.description: A rounded or square-corner lowered application surface with one compact inset and a vertical content stack.
entries.purpose: Group a vertical list of application content on a visually lowered surface with one owned 8px inset and an explicit rounded or square-corner shape.
useWhen: A main content region or nested work area needs a darker/lowered background and one compact inset around a vertical stack.
Use the default rounded shape for an inset surface; choose square for a flush or edge-to-edge application area.
avoidWhen: Do not use it merely to add padding, as a substitute for Pane anatomy, or around children that already own the same outer surface.

alternatives.when: Use layout roles for pane, toolbar, scroll, and ordinary content-stack ownership.

accessibility: Pass ariaLabel only when the surface is a distinct named region; otherwise it remains a non-landmark grouping.

notes: The root owns one 8px inset and vertical gap; children own their borders and internal geometry.

entries.name: Toolbar
entries.description: Leading, centered, and trailing toolbar composition.
entries.purpose: Leading, centered, and trailing toolbar composition.
useWhen: Compose application chrome or a page, panel, or dialog heading with leading, center, and trailing regions.
Use typed hideBelow/showBelow lengths with wireToolbarVisibility(root) for per-item toolbar priority; keep primary actions available and provide a showBelow overflow alternative.
avoidWhen: Do not use it as a generic wrapper when no toolbar or heading relationship exists.

variants: scroll dividers when named as wireScrollDividers targets chrome
stacked zones at compact or narrow widths
content-driven wrap that keeps a heading title whole
center priority for an expanded center control
trailing priority for an expanded trailing control at compact or narrow widths

entries.name: ToolbarControlGroup
entries.description: Typed toolbar groups for buttons, semantic action links, compact mixed controls, selected states, dropdown surfaces, and avatar controls.
entries.purpose: Provide complete toolbar action geometry through configuration, including semantic anchors, overflow containment, and dropdown menu insets without application CSS.
useWhen: Group related controls inside a toolbar with a supported visual treatment.
Use ToolbarActionLink for navigation or external resources that must retain native anchor semantics inside a group.

Fill it with plain <button> controls (the group styles > button fully); use wa-button only for a Web Awesome feature. A popup menu is a PopupMenu in a single group with nestedDropdown; it renders its own trigger, so never hand-write wa-dropdown markup. Each control stays whole: an icon sits beside its label on one row and no trigger gets a fixed width. Use overflow=wrap for independent links that should move as whole actions to another row on narrow surfaces.
For an avatar control, set content=avatar and avatarImage instead of inserting an img; one button paints the group and multiple buttons paint only the pressed highlight.
In a Workbench or CollapsiblePanel toolbar, mark a group relocateOnCollapse to keep it available in the work-area toolbar when the panel closes; place it directly or in an array in any toolbar zone.
Use tileTone for a contained single group containing only a direct decorative SVG icon; interactive or mixed groups retain their existing control chrome.
Set expandedOverflow=visible on an expanded search to anchor application suggestions, date pickers, or help below the group without overriding its geometry.
Use typed hideBelow/showBelow lengths with wireToolbarVisibility(root) for per-item toolbar priority; keep primary actions available and provide a showBelow overflow alternative.

Do not reach for wa-button for an ordinary control inside the group — a plain <button> is the default and avoids the Web Awesome dependency.

stateAttributes.meaning: Preserves actual CSS visibility while rendering removes a transient parent marker, preventing geometry-driven render feedback.

entries.name: Surface scaffolds
entries.description: Typed Web Awesome dialog preferred widths and viewport bounds, presentation, and popup inset composition.
entries.purpose: Configure recurring dialog and popup geometry without consumer ::part() overrides.
useWhen: A Web Awesome dialog or dropdown needs a standard size, presentation, body/footer inset, or list-compatible menu inset.
A dialog body should compose rows, sections, or aligned bare prose through List and ListInsetText.
A modal needs a typed preferred width, viewport gutter, or dynamic viewport-bounded height cap while retaining native body scrolling and footer actions.
avoidWhen: Do not use it as a generic layout wrapper or to replace application-owned modal state and focus lifecycle.
Do not stack a dialog body inset around children that already own List or content-item geometry; use bodyInset none.
variants: typed modal preferred width, viewport gutter, and maximum height, including viewport cap
none, compact, or comfortable body and footer inset
standard, compact, or zero-inset popup menu
accessibility: Supply the wrapped wa-dialog label and retain Web Awesome's native modal and focus behavior.
Use popup surfaces only for real dropdown menus with named triggers.

entries.name: FloatingToolbar
entries.description: A transparent, forced-dark toolbar that floats over its container's content.
entries.purpose: A transparent, forced-dark toolbar that floats over its container's content.
useWhen: Float a small cluster of controls (e.g. a drawer restore) over scrolling content without covering dialogs.
avoidWhen: Do not use for a primary page or panel toolbar, or for anything that must sit above overlays (it is not top-layer).
accessibility: Give the toolbar an accessible name (label is required — it exposes role="toolbar").

entries.name: ToolbarText
entries.description: Extra-large through extra-small toolbar identity text.
entries.purpose: Extra-large through extra-small toolbar identity text.
useWhen: Render toolbar identity or heading text at a supported hierarchy size; pass headingLevel for heading semantics.
Use action for an editable toolbar title: it renders a native button that shrinks and ellipsizes beside sibling status chips.
Use tone=dark for title or filename text on a loud toolbar surface, matching dark ToolbarControlGroups.
Use typed hideBelow/showBelow lengths with wireToolbarVisibility(root) for per-item toolbar priority; keep primary actions available and provide a showBelow overflow alternative.
avoidWhen: Do not omit headingLevel when the text is the page or section heading.

Large, default, and small are intentionally quiet toolbar identity text in default tone. Use xlarge-fixed for a normal-color toolbar heading at the fixed font-l step; use Text with an h2-h6 variant for a content subsection title, or ListHeader for a list or menu section.

alternatives.when: Use Text variant h2-h6 for a normal-color subsection title in content rather than toolbar identity.
Use ListHeader for a list or menu section label with a count, badge, action, or disclosure.

appOwns: the delegated action handler and display-to-input editing swap
variants: typed hideBelow/showBelow thresholds at the nearest Toolbar content width
accessibility: Plain text is not a heading; pass headingLevel to expose role=heading + aria-level for a page/section title.
Actionable text is a native button with its full text as its accessible name; action cannot be combined with headingLevel, placeholder, or wrap.

stateAttributes.name: data-toolbar-width-hidden
stateAttributes.on: ToolbarText, ToolbarControlGroup and its paired busy status
stateAttributes.meaning: True when typed hideBelow/showBelow thresholds hide this item at the nearest Toolbar content width. Re-applied after rendering; disposal restores prior markers.

stateAttributes.name: data-toolbar-visibility-probe
stateAttributes.on: private aria-hidden measurement boxes under Toolbar
stateAttributes.meaning: Internal out-of-flow CSS length resolver; created and removed by wireToolbarVisibility.

stateAttributes.name: data-morph-preserve
stateAttributes.on: private aria-hidden measurement boxes and visibility state children
stateAttributes.meaning: Keeps helper-owned geometry and state across Kerf renders; replacement and explicit removal are repaired, and disposal removes them.

stateAttributes.name: data-toolbar-visibility-state
stateAttributes.on: private hidden children of width-managed items and paired busy statuses
stateAttributes.meaning: Preserves actual CSS visibility while rendering removes a transient parent marker, preventing geometry-driven render feedback.

entries.name: Text
entries.description: Semantic native text plus a FieldLabel heading for read-only field previews that matches themed Web Awesome form labels.
entries.purpose: Render paragraph semantics by default, h1 through h6 when selected, or geometry-free inline secondary text as a span while independently configuring quiet or danger tone, compact through extra-large size, or monospace font.
useWhen: Render ordinary application headings or paragraphs with native document semantics, or inline secondary text inside rows, labels, and table cells.
Render FieldLabel over a read-only or click-to-edit preview that replaces a Web Awesome form control.
avoidWhen: Do not use Text for toolbar identity or title content; use ToolbarText inside a Toolbar zone.
Do not choose a heading variant for visual size alone; preserve the document heading hierarchy.
appOwns: FieldLabel copy, preview/edit state, and aria-labelledby association
variants: p, h1 through h6, or inline span semantic variant
compact, default, large, or xlarge size
flush item geometry and tight line height
controlMargins selects exterior 8px gutters with canonical physical Sides
accessibility: Text renders a native paragraph by default; choose an h1 through h6 variant by document outline rather than appearance, or span for inline secondary text.
Ordinary global, data, and ARIA attributes pass through to the native element.
Choose tone, size, and font independently of the heading level so appearance does not distort the document outline.
FieldLabel is plain text, not a native label; give it an id and associate the preview group with aria-labelledby.

notes: Block Text variants reset native margins and add a 1px transparent border plus the standard 8px item padding; flush removes the border and padding. Tight line height is available for compact copy. Span has no margin by default, border, or padding. FieldLabel mirrors the themed Web Awesome label typography, 9px inline inset, and bottom gap.

controlMargins adds the shared control gutter outside selected physical edges without changing border or padding; avoid duplicating a parent inset. Spans retain inline display and native inline margin behavior.

entries.name: Headers
entries.description: Page, dialog, and definition-list hierarchy.
entries.purpose: Page, dialog, and definition-list hierarchy.
useWhen: Compose page, dialog, and definition-list hierarchy from their distinct primitives.
avoidWhen: Do not reuse one header primitive only because its typography looks similar.
accessibility: Preserve heading and description relationships for the containing surface.

entries.name: ValueTable
entries.description: Key/value rows with optional icons.
entries.purpose: Key/value rows with optional icons and aligned separators.
useWhen: Present read-only label/value facts as a semantic definition list, optionally with a 24px leading icon.
avoidWhen: Do not use for editable fields or row/column tabular data.
accessibility: Name ValueTable with its label; ValueTableRow supplies dt/dd semantics, and row icons stay decorative unless meaning requires an accessible label.

entries.name: Row
entries.description: A horizontal flex row with physical-axis alignment, side-selectable text/control insets, a typed xs gap by default, flex participation, and opt-in wrapping.
entries.purpose: Arrange related content horizontally with consistent spacing, optional physical-side text/control insets, and explicit left/center/right/full plus top/middle/bottom/full/baseline alignment instead of application-owned flex wrappers.
useWhen: Arrange a group of sibling components horizontally.
Choose physical horizontal distribution and vertical alignment without writing one-off flex CSS.
Use a finite flex keyword or the flex() builder when Row participates in a flexible parent layout.
Allow a bounded group to wrap while retaining the same typed gap and alignment contract.
Apply the standard text or control inset to selected physical sides without an application wrapper.
avoidWhen: Do not use Row when content belongs in a semantic list or when a named-zone component such as Toolbar owns the composition.
Do not pass raw CSS strings to gap or flex, mix their distinct grammars, or use s/xl spacing steps without a deliberate exception.
Do not use alignment to replace semantic grouping or responsive relocation.

alternatives.when: Use List when the main layout axis is vertical.
Use Toolbar when content belongs to named leading, center, and trailing application-chrome zones.

variants: left/center/right/full horizontal alignment with l/c/r/f and flex aliases
top/middle/bottom/full vertical alignment with t/m/c/b/f and flex aliases, plus baseline alignment
boolean, finite-keyword, or typed CssFlex flex
top/right/bottom/left text and control inset combinations
fill: the layout root fills a definite-height parent
rootAttributes: safe data-* metadata on the root
accessibility: Row adds layout only and no grouping role; children retain responsibility for native or ARIA semantics.
Wrapping must preserve a readable source and focus order.

notes: Row adds no margin or border. textInsets adds the full 17px content inset and controlInsets adds 8px on selected physical sides; text wins when both select a side.

entries.name: Grid
entries.description: Equal-width columns with a fixed count or a minimum-width responsive mode, typed gaps, physical-side text/control insets, and optional flex participation.
entries.purpose: Arrange related siblings in equal-width columns with either a fixed count or automatic container-width collapse.
useWhen: Arrange related siblings into a fixed positive number of equal-width columns.
Fit equal-width columns down to a typed minimum and collapse as the container narrows.
Prevent wider intrinsic content from making one fractional track wider than its peers.
Use a finite flex keyword or the flex() builder when Grid participates in a flexible parent layout.
avoidWhen: Do not use Grid for intrinsic, asymmetric, spanning, or masonry tracks; use application-owned CSS grid.
Do not use Grid when columns need a user-operable separator; use ResizableRegion.
Do not combine fixed columns with minColumnWidth; choose one layout mode.
Do not pass raw CSS strings to gap or flex, mix their distinct grammars, or use s/xl spacing steps without a deliberate exception.

alternatives.when: Use Row for one horizontal flex line, alignment, or wrapping rather than fixed equal tracks.
Use List when the main layout axis is vertical.
Use ResizableRegion when people must adjust the boundary between tracks.

appOwns: fixed column count or responsive minimum width
typed gap, flex, and physical-side inset choices
variants: typed minimum column width with automatic container-width collapse
boolean, finite-keyword, or typed CssFlex flex
top/right/bottom/left text and control inset combinations
fill: the layout root fills a definite-height parent
rootAttributes: safe data-* metadata on the root
selectionMode=multiple: labeled multi-select grid for ContentItem tiles
accessibility: Grid adds no role by default; selectionMode=multiple requires ariaLabel and supplies a multi-select grid for ContentItem row/gridcell tiles.
wireContentItems uses rendered tile positions for Left/Right/Up/Down and reaches the first or last tile with Home/End.
Responsive column-count changes preserve source and focus order.

notes: textInsets adds 17px and controlInsets adds 8px on selected physical sides; text wins on overlap.
Fixed tracks use minmax(0, 1fr); responsive tracks use auto-fit with a minimum width capped at 100%, preserving equal distribution without narrow overflow.

entries.name: Spacer
entries.description: A decorative, non-shrinking fixed gap or flexible main-axis spacer with typed physical width and height.
entries.purpose: Express an intentional empty dimension or consume remaining flex space without application-owned spacer markup or raw CSS lengths.
useWhen: Reserve a fixed empty width or height from the UI spacing scale inside a layout.
Push siblings to opposite ends of a Row or other flex container by passing flex.
Use a typed CssLength when the finite spacing scale cannot express the required dimension.
avoidWhen: Do not use Spacer for ordinary rhythm between siblings; prefer Row.gap or List.gap so the parent owns repeated spacing.
Do not use Spacer to compensate for component-owned padding, margin, alignment, or responsive layout defects.
Do not pass raw CSS strings to width or height.

alternatives.when: Use Row.gap when every horizontal sibling needs the same repeated separation.
Use List.gap when every vertical sibling needs the same repeated separation.

appOwns: whether the empty space carries structural meaning
whether the spacer fills the flex main axis
variants: fixed typed CssLength width and/or height
accessibility: Spacer is always decorative and hidden from the accessibility tree.
Spacer must not contain content or become an interaction target.

notes: A fixed Spacer does not shrink. flex changes its flex shorthand from 0 0 auto to 1 1 auto; width and height remain physical dimensions.

entries.name: List
entries.description: A vertical stack with physical-axis alignment, side-selectable text/control insets, optional typed token/length gap, flex growth, vertical scrolling, and independently selectable divider edges.
entries.purpose: Standardize vertical component layout, optional physical-side text/control insets, and scroll/divider ownership instead of repeating ad-hoc flex-column wrappers.
useWhen: Arrange component rows or sections in a vertical stretch-aligned stack.
Let one bounded list own vertical scrolling, flex growth, or one or more physical-edge dividers.
Choose a finite gap shorthand such as xs or m, or compose a typed length with @kerfjs/ui/css-values when the spacing scale is insufficient.
Use a finite flex keyword or the flex() builder when List participates in flexible layout.
Apply the standard text or control inset to selected physical sides without an application wrapper.
Align children horizontally or distribute them vertically with the same physical alignment vocabulary as Row.
Use selectionMode="multiple" and ariaLabel to group selectable rich ContentItem rows in a multi-select grid.
avoidWhen: Do not use List as semantic list markup; use ul/ol when list semantics are required and apply layout deliberately.
Do not create nested scroll owners or use divider sides as a substitute for meaningful grouping.
Do not pass raw CSS strings to gap or flex, mix their distinct grammars, or use the off-rhythm s/xl spacing steps without a deliberate exception.
appOwns: the bounded height needed for scrolling
typed gap, flex, alignment, and divider choices
the accessible label and selection state of a multi-select grid
variants: boolean, finite-keyword, or typed CssFlex flex
top/right/bottom/left text and control inset combinations
fill: the layout root fills a definite-height parent
rootAttributes: safe data-* metadata on the root
scroll dividers when named as wireScrollDividers targets chrome
multi-select grid for rich ContentItem rows
accessibility: List adds layout only and no list role by default; selectionMode="multiple" makes it an aria-multiselectable grid with a required ariaLabel for selectable ContentItem rows.
Give a scrollable List a bounded block size and keep keyboard focus visible as its contents scroll.

notes: List adds no margin. dividerSides draws selected physical edges without changing geometry; textInsets adds the full 17px content inset and controlInsets adds 8px on selected sides, with text winning on overlap.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-overflow
stateAttributes.meaning: The physical edges, in canonical t/r/b/l order, beyond which content is scrolled out of view; absent when nothing is hidden (content that fits never reports its far edges). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-divider
stateAttributes.on: a List named as targets chrome
stateAttributes.meaning: The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which this chrome currently draws its scroll divider: the side facing the scroller while content is hidden beyond it. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: ListHeader
entries.description: Configurable section headings with five independent label sizes, full-width or shrink-wrapped inline presentation, semantic count/status indicators, density, group dividers, a logical-end action, disclosure states, and protected native-popover trigger metadata.
entries.purpose: Fill the available section width by default, or shrink-wrap without outer geometry when inline, while splitting a dormant title and mutually exclusive semantic count or badge from an optional logical-end action with an 18px visual; disclosure mode renders the title cluster as a button with a default production DisclosureArrow.
useWhen: Label a navigation section with an optional semantic count, non-count badge, action, or disclosure state; toggle mode supplies an 18px DisclosureArrow unless actionIcon replaces it.
avoidWhen: Do not concatenate a section count into label or pass numeric content through badge; use count with its required localized countLabel.
Do not use as a page or dialog title.
appOwns: valid count and localized count label
variants: label sizes xs, sm (default), m, l, xl
neutral, accent, pop, or danger indicator tone
before, after, or paired group divider
accessibility: A valid count is hidden as duplicate visual text and its required localized countLabel joins the owned heading or disclosure-button accessible name; zero remains visible.

The application controls and updates disclosure state and the revealed content; the default DisclosureArrow mirrors expanded while the button name stays stable. triggerAttributes can describe the controlled relationship but cannot replace the owned accessible name or expanded state.

entries.name: ListActionRow
entries.description: Configurable navigation rows with structured labels, status/busy metadata, density, group dividers, and sibling primary/trailing native-button actions.
entries.purpose: Keep a selectable primary row action and an independently named trailing action as sibling native controls inside one noninteractive visual row.
useWhen: A navigation or item row needs both a primary selectable action and an independently focusable trailing action.
avoidWhen: Use ListItem when trailing content is dormant metadata; use AppTab only for tablist semantics and ToolbarControlGroup only for toolbar controls.
Do not inject declaration strings; use className, public tokens, and cataloged component props for application styling.

alternatives.when: Trailing content is noninteractive.
The primary control selects a tabpanel inside TabBar.

variants: before, after, or paired group divider
accessibility: The noninteractive root contains two sibling native buttons in primary-then-trailing focus order; each button has its own action, item identity, accessible name, and disabled state.

Selection semantics are exposed only by the primary button; label, icon, and trailingActionIcon are dormant SafeHtml and must not contain interactive descendants; never place an interactive descendant in ListItem.trailing.

entries.name: ListItem
entries.description: Configurable native-button action rows and native-anchor navigation rows with structured labels, status/busy metadata, density, group dividers, protected domain metadata hooks, and rounded-boundary overflow clipping.
entries.purpose: Selectable, disabled, trailing, and multiline action or link rows.
useWhen: Render a selectable, disabled, trailing, or multiline sidebar action row whose descendants must remain clipped to the rounded row boundary; use ListItemLink when the destination has an href and needs native link activation.
avoidWhen: Do not use for an ordinary inline link, form button, isolated ARIA menuitem, or an interactive trailing action; use ListActionRow for sibling row actions.
Do not inject declaration strings; use className, public tokens, and cataloged component props for application styling.

alternatives.when: The trailing region must be independently interactive.

variants: centered icon beside a multiline label
before, after, or paired group divider
accessibility: ListItem uses native button activation and pressed maps to aria-pressed; ListItemLink uses native anchor activation and external opens a new tab with safe rel and an announced default label. Both map selected to aria-current; disabled or loading links omit href and leave the tab order. rootAttributes cannot add role=menuitem or replace owned ARIA; trailing is dormant content and must not contain controls.

notes: Public resting, hover, and selected text, fill, and border tokens can be scoped to a row or its containing list without changing the default tones.

entries.name: ListInsetControl
entries.description: Insets selected physical sides of a self-bordered control in a pane/list content region.
entries.purpose: Apply the standard 8px outer margin to all physical sides of a self-bordered control by default, or only the sides selected with the canonical Sides contract.
useWhen: Place a control that carries its own border and padding (an input, a wa-* control) in a pane/list content region so its edges align with .kui-content items.
avoidWhen: Do not wrap a component that already owns its content-item margin (ListItem, StateBanner, …) — that double-insets it. Use ListInsetText for bare text.
appOwns: the wrapped control and its behavior
accessibility: A layout wrapper only; it adds no role or name — the wrapped control keeps its own.

entries.name: ListInsetText
entries.description: Gives selected physical sides of bare text the content-item geometry so it lines up with bordered items.
entries.purpose: Apply the full 8px margin + 1px transparent border + 8px padding to all physical sides of bare text by default, or only the sides selected with the canonical Sides contract.
useWhen: Line a plain text element up with bordered .kui-content items — it adds the 8px margin, 1px transparent border, and 8px padding the text lacks.
avoidWhen: Do not use it to wrap an interactive control (use ListInsetControl), or a component that already owns its content-item geometry.
accessibility: A layout wrapper only; it adds no role or name.

entries.name: ContentItem
entries.description: One self-contained content child with shared geometry plus typed transparent, surface, or semantic appearance, frame, and shape choices.
entries.purpose: Render one self-contained .kui-content child that owns its 8px inline margin, real 1px border, 8px padding, radius, and optional coordinated surface colors.
useWhen: An ordinary surface-like child of a Pane or .kui-content stack needs the shared content-item geometry so its content edge lands at the standard 17px inset.
A content item marks a real distinction and must read as visibly bounded: pass frame="framed" (the border is always reserved, so geometry does not change).
A content item needs the base surface or a coordinated semantic status treatment: pass appearance="surface" or a semantic appearance such as success or danger.
A content item should follow a pill control's 22px radius: pass shape="pill".
A selectable rich card needs nested controls: use selectionMode="multiple" inside a labeled List multi-select grid.
avoidWhen: Do not wrap a component that already owns content-item geometry (ListItem, ListHeader, StateBanner, Toolbar, ValueTable) or pad around a ContentItem; either double-insets.
Do not frame an item only to make it look contained; hierarchy comes from alignment, spacing, and type first.
Do not use its surface appearance for a lowered inset panel around a stack; use SunkenPanel for that structure.
Do not use it for bare text alone; use ListInsetText, which adds the same inset without claiming a surface.

alternatives.when: Use ListInsetText when bare text only needs to align with neighboring content items.
Use SunkenPanel for a lowered, filled surface around a vertical stack.
Place ContentItem children in a Pane or .kui-content stack, which owns the 24px major rhythm.

appOwns: whether the item marks a real distinction that warrants a visible frame
whether the item needs a surface or semantic appearance
whether the item is a programmatic focus target
the selection set and Shift/Cmd extension for multi-select rich cards
variants: neutral, info, pop, success, warning, or danger semantic item
accessibility: An ordinary item adds no role or name; pass ariaLabel only when the item is a distinct named region (it then renders role="region").
focusTarget makes the item a programmatic focus target (tabindex="-1", never a tab stop), such as a NavStack view's data-nav-focus target.
The frame is decorative and never the only signal of state.

selectionMode="multiple" renders a focusable row with aria-selected and a gridcell for nested controls; place it in a labeled List selectionMode="multiple" grid. wireContentItems moves focus among rows with Up/Down and Home/End while nested controls retain those keys. Guard the app's delegated card action with isContentItemActivation so a nested control does not select the row.

notes: The 1px border is always reserved; transparent items paint it only when frame="framed", while surface and semantic appearances coordinate its color with their background and foreground.

entries.name: Application tabs
entries.description: Controlled document tabs with application-owned state and panels.
entries.purpose: Show AppTab and TabBar in a complete controlled composition.
useWhen: Compose application state, panels, actions, overflow, and reordering around TabBar and AppTab.
avoidWhen: Use SegmentedControl instead for a compact local choice.
accessibility: Keep one selected tab synchronized with one named tabpanel and retain the wireTabBars disposer.

entries.name: AppTab
entries.description: Roving-tabindex-ready tabs with typed compact, segmented, icon-only, drop-target, pinned, and name-overflow presentations.
entries.purpose: Render a controlled application tab with compact or icon-only presentation, a visible drop target, optional full-name display, and an optional pinned leading position.
useWhen: Render one controlled application tab inside TabBar.
avoidWhen: Do not render alone or use for a compact settings choice.
variants: label maximum width and ellipsis or visible name overflow
pinned leading position within a scrolling tablist
accessibility: Compose in a tablist and pair with an application-owned tabpanel.
Keep closeIcon decorative and free of interactive descendants; the owning close button supplies its accessible name and interaction.
Use rootAttributes only for application data-* metadata; component-owned identity, state, action, and role semantics are protected at runtime.

entries.name: TabBar
entries.description: Controlled tab strips with typed presentation and allocation, a scroll-owning tab region, an optional adjacent trailing action, and a separately pinned far-edge end action.
entries.purpose: Controlled tab strips whose tabs shrink and scroll while fixed leading, trailing, and far-edge end actions remain visible.
useWhen: Switch application tabpanels with optional overflow, closing, and reordering.
avoidWhen: Do not use for a compact local toggle or a long value list.
variants: standalone Web Awesome action in trailing or end
overflow dividers on each side with tabs scrolled out of view (wired by wireScrollDividers)
accessibility: Keep exactly one selected tab at tabindex 0 and preserve the wiring keyboard model.
Call wireTabBars for keyboard focus and selection, including the pinned leading tab's WebKit RTL scroll correction.

notes: TabBar owns inline flex allocation: tabs shrink and scroll, an adjacent trailing action follows the tab strip, and the end action stays pinned at the far edge; leading, trailing, and end actions do not shrink.

stateAttributes.name: data-tab-dragging
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" on the tab being dragged.

stateAttributes.name: data-tab-drop-position
stateAttributes.meaning: "before" or "after" on the tab under the pointer: where the dragged tab would land.

stateAttributes.name: data-tab-autoscroll
stateAttributes.meaning: "start" or "end" while a drag near that edge auto-scrolls the strip.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-overflow
stateAttributes.meaning: The physical edges, in canonical t/r/b/l order, beyond which content is scrolled out of view; absent when nothing is hidden (content that fits never reports its far edges). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

stateAttributes.name: data-scroll-divider
stateAttributes.on: chrome named in wireScrollDividers targets (a TabBar strip has none)
stateAttributes.meaning: The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which that chrome currently draws its scroll divider. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

entries.name: SegmentedControl
entries.description: Controlled exclusive choices in toolbar, rounded-rectangle, and pill presentations.
entries.purpose: Controlled exclusive choices in toolbar, rounded-rectangle, and pill presentations.
useWhen: Expose a small controlled exclusive choice set.
avoidWhen: Do not use for tabpanel semantics or many choices.
accessibility: Keep choice labels meaningful and every enabled native button in sequential Tab order.

entries.name: TokenSearchField
entries.description: Token-controlled, optionally collapsible search editor with ordered, editable, removable filter chips.
entries.purpose: Token-controlled, optionally collapsible search editor with ordered, editable, removable filter chips.
useWhen: Combine DOM-owned free text with ordered editable/removable filter tokens in one searchbox.
Enable collapsible mode when an empty, unfocused search should reduce to one iconic action, standalone or inside a toolbar group.
Use presentation="form-field" for a structured search query beside Web Awesome form controls, with a visible label, optional hint, and required marker.
avoidWhen: Do not use for ordinary text input or separately labeled filter controls.
appOwns: the grammar and evaluation callback when using the optional managed model, or parsing, suggestions, tokens, and query execution in manual mode
the revision that rebuilds the DOM-owned editor for a programmatic text replacement
optional override of the collapsible expand/collapse/focus, which wireTokenSearchFields manages by default (adopt an app expanded signal, opt out per behavior, or drive it via the returned handle)
validation of a required form-field value
variants: visible form-field label, hint, and required marker
accessibility: Announce result changes when useful and keep tokens atomic during editing.

Keep leading and trailing controls aligned to the first text line while content wraps. Managed Clear restores replacement focus before the next input task, preserving immediate typing and later focus handoffs without a frame delay.

Wire Enter to submit without inserting a contenteditable line break and preserve focus plus the text-relative caret across controlled keyboard chip deletion before the next keystroke. Select All deletion preserves managed open state and replacement focus; persist both edited query and tokens. Visual wrapping remains available.

In collapsible mode, wireTokenSearchFields manages this by default: activating the trigger reveals the searchbox and moves focus into it, Escape on an empty field collapses and returns focus to the trigger, and focus leaving an empty field collapses it; each behavior is individually opt-out.

The form-field presentation associates its visible label and optional hint with the searchbox, exposes aria-required when required, and lets wireTokenSearchFields focus the editor from a label click. The app validates required input.

stateAttributes.name: data-token-search-text
stateAttributes.meaning: Marks the plain-text span the helper inserts when the editor is emptied.

stateAttributes.name: data-empty
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" on that span while it holds no text.

stateAttributes.name: data-placeholder-visible
stateAttributes.meaning: Tracks whether the DOM-owned editor is empty so its placeholder stays outside the editable area.

entries.name: ResizableRegion
entries.description: Pointer and keyboard-operable split region with a customizable handle icon.
entries.purpose: Pointer and keyboard-operable split region with a customizable handle icon.
useWhen: Provide a controlled user-resizable application pane.
avoidWhen: Do not use for static columns; use CSS grid.
variants: inline, overlay, or hidden responsive presentation
accessibility: Preserve separator naming, value ARIA, and keyboard behavior.
Keep handleIcon decorative and free of interactive descendants; the separator owns focus, naming, and pointer/keyboard interaction.

notes: The region delegates visible separator geometry and hit-area padding to its orientation-specific handle.

stateAttributes.name: data-handle-inset
stateAttributes.meaning: Present while a clipping edge clamps the region: the handle and its focus ring sit inside the region instead of overhanging that edge.

stateAttributes.name: data-resizing
stateAttributes.meaning: "true" during an active pointer drag of the handle.

entries.name: Select
entries.description: Controlled Web Awesome select with typed single or multiple values, disabled choices, optional bulk actions, and form, toolbar, navigation, compact, icon-only, truncating, hint, and grouped-choice presentations.
entries.purpose: Choose one or more controlled values, keep unavailable choices visible, and optionally select all enabled choices or clear a multiple selection.
useWhen: Choose a controlled value from a moderate or long list, including grouped and icon-bearing choices.

Color an optional choice icon with a CssForegroundColor: uiColor() with a foreground token such as success-on-quiet, foregroundColorVar() for an app-owned property, or foregroundColor() for a direct custom CSS color. Fill tokens such as success are backgrounds that leave the icon nearly invisible, so they, lengths, raw color strings, and unqualified colorVar() values are rejected.
Use the default content-sized menu for long option labels; native popup shifting keeps it within 10px viewport gutters. fitMenu instead matches trigger width and wraps labels.
avoidWhen: Do not use for commands or a small choice set that should stay visible.
variants: fit-content, max-content, or fill trigger width
custom selected content typography and ellipsis
disabled choice with an optional reason
opt-in select-all and clear actions for multiple selection
multiple icon-only filter trigger with a fixed triggerIcon
accessibility: Verify the live value, standard events, focus, and rendered output.
A nonempty label names the internal combobox; otherwise ariaLabel supplies a visually hidden label without adding control height, including custom selected content.
Hint text is visible below the control through Web Awesome's native hint relationship; placeholderText remains the empty value inside the closed control.

Import select/register once; its scoped lifecycle adapter keeps the latest open/close request authoritative across animation reversals, canceled transitions, and removal. Do not add consumer popup timing or position repairs.

With multiple, the popup stays open while choices toggle (pointer, Enter, or Space) and closes on an outside press, Escape, or focus leaving; each chosen option shows a check, and the closed control summarizes the chosen labels in choice order.

Disabled choices stay visible but cannot be selected; disabledReason exposes a tooltip. A multiple Select can opt in to localized select-all and clear buttons, which skip disabled choices and publish ordinary input/change events for changed values.

A multiple icon-only trigger shows its fixed triggerIcon and, while any choice is chosen, an aria-hidden count Badge; the combobox's accessible name ends with the chosen labels in choice order, and its hidden value stays empty.

Once registered, an icon-only trigger (single or multiple) shows an aria-hidden Web Awesome help tag repeating its accessible name (a single Select adds its current choice) after a 500ms hover and at once on keyboard focus; it hides while the popup is open, on a press, and on Escape, and never joins aria-labelledby. usageExamples.title: Pointer anchored context menu
usageExamples.description: Keep the row's visible disabled action separate from the context menu anchor. Find the menu root with a stable data attribute.
usageExamples.code:
<PopupMenu
  context
  label="Demand actions"
  rootAttributes={{ 'data-demand-menu': '' }}
  items={[{ label: 'Open', action: 'open-demand' }]}
/>
// In the app's row wiring:
row.addEventListener('contextmenu', (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  const menu = row.querySelector('[data-demand-menu]') as PopupMenuElement;
  openPopupMenuAt(menu, event.clientX, event.clientY);
});
// Call closePopupMenu(menu) when the app needs to dismiss it.

useWhen: A workspace sidebar needs the shared toolbar/content/footer pane model, 24px major section rhythm, and 44px row and utility-action targets.
avoidWhen: Use ordinary links when menu selection, section, and sidebar anatomy do not apply.
accessibility: Native buttons retain names, current state, sequential focus, and disclosure state; rows and standalone footer actions remain at least 44px tall.

entries.name: Workspace header
entries.purpose: Page identity with primary, secondary, and overflow actions that relocate at narrow widths.
useWhen: A workspace page needs one primary heading and a small prioritized action set.
avoidWhen: Use a smaller local heading when the page does not need actions or persistent identity.
accessibility: Heading order and action focus order remain stable when controls wrap.

entries.name: List-detail dialog
entries.purpose: Production modal laid out as a workbench: a full-height SplitView list sidebar with its own toolbar beside a full-height detail column that carries the primary title, close control, and record actions; a full-screen drill-down on compact devices.
useWhen: A focused task compares several records without leaving the current workspace.
avoidWhen: Use a page when the task needs a durable route or substantially more working space.
accessibility: Web Awesome owns modal focus, Escape, and the labeled header with its close control; the application adapter restores the invoking control after hide, and the compact NavStack back control returns to the list.

entries.name: Composer form
entries.purpose: One visible publishing-form surface with Toolbar heading hierarchy, fields and actions on the shared 8px control gutter, 24px major rhythm, and a conditional StateBanner as its only nested semantic surface.
useWhen: A short form needs one coherent surface, consistent field/action rhythm, and persistent validation feedback.
avoidWhen: Do not turn each form section into another visible card or use the recipe as a generic form engine or transport abstraction.
accessibility: The form references its ToolbarText title and supporting-summary ids; production fields own labels and help; invalid submission creates an assertive persistent StateBanner while successful submission creates a polite persistent banner.

entries.name: List workspace states
entries.purpose: Deterministic loading, empty, populated, stale refresh, and error states around one stable list workspace.
useWhen: A list surface must communicate initial load, absence, background refresh, failure, and recovery.
avoidWhen: Do not replace domain rows with a generic component or use transient toasts as the only error record.
accessibility: Busy, polite, and assertive states use the appropriate production feedback semantics.

entries.name: Compact toolbar choices and actions
entries.purpose: A compact toolbar that distinguishes grouped commands, a visible exclusive choice, a longer Select, and one ordinary action.
useWhen: A dense workspace toolbar mixes a few distinct control semantics.
avoidWhen: Do not group unrelated actions or use buttons to imitate selection controls.
accessibility: Each control retains its own native name, pressed/value state, and keyboard contract.

entries.name: Navigation stack
entries.purpose: A push/pop navigation stack drill-down with animated slides and a live device class.
useWhen: A flow drills from a list into detail and back on one pane, at any device size or inside a dialog.
avoidWhen: Use SplitView when a list and its detail should show together on roomy classes.
accessibility: The back control is a real button; reduced motion collapses the slide to instant.

entries.name: Loading inspector
entries.purpose: A record inspector whose per-record values load asynchronously — every value-bearing component takes a shared placeholder flag, so the same chrome renders a faithful loading state and then the populated record.
useWhen: A detail or inspector view must render its real chrome while its per-record values are still loading, then swap to the populated record without duplicating markup.
avoidWhen: Do not hand-build a separate empty-state layout, and do not use it for known progress — use LoadingSpinner for that.
accessibility: Each component marks itself aria-busy and disables its own controls while loading; the composition keeps labels and structure stable across the transition.

entries.name: Collapsible sidebar
entries.purpose: A mini app frame whose left navigation rail and bottom activity drawer are standalone CollapsiblePanels driven by wireSidebar: per-side collapse/expand toggles, focus move-in and restore, a dismissable compact overlay, and per-panel persistence.
useWhen: A rail or drawer must collapse and expand outside a full Workbench shell, keeping the app's collapsed signals, sizes, and content while the wire owns toggle, focus, the compact overlay, and persistence.
avoidWhen: Use the Workbench layout when the whole screen is a three-pane shell; use an ordinary always-visible sidebar when it never collapses.
accessibility: Each panel is a labeled aside that is aria-hidden while collapsed; toggles carry aria-expanded and the standard per-side glyph; while compact an open panel is an overlay with a backdrop, Escape and backdrop-click dismiss, and a trapped Tab ring.
